summary.headline: IFB Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.0% to INR 1,456 crore and PAT to INR 33.7 crore, but FY26 commodity and forex hits of INR 84 crore were only partly offset.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.0% YoY to INR 1,456 crore, with PBDIT margin at 5.5% against 5.3% a year earlier. PAT rose to INR 33.7 crore from INR 22.3 crore after a INR 0.58 crore Labour Code exceptional charge. For FY26, revenue grew 10% to INR 5,476 crore, while PAT rose 3.5% to INR 133.3 crore and PAT margin fell to 2.4% from 2.6%. Management said INR 67 crore of the INR 84 crore FY26 commodity and forex hit was recovered through cost initiatives and price increases. April-May commodity and forex headwinds of about INR 49 crore are only partly offset (INR 29 crore from cost initiatives so far).

segments.name: Home Appliances
segments.commentary: Management said front loaders grew about 21% in Q4 and 7-8% for FY26, top loaders grew about 19% for the year, and microwaves grew double digits in Q4. AC growth was muted after the Q1 FY26 monsoon-related dip, and OEM sales fell about 5% in FY26.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue CAGR of about 13% over five years, with management targeting 20-25% growth over the next 2-3 years and an EBITDA margin of 17-18% against about 15% today. FY26 new order wins were about INR 153 crore against a INR 250 crore target.

segments.name: Associate (refrigeration)
segments.commentary: Share of loss of INR 1.4 crore for FY26 from the refrigeration associate; management declined to discuss the business further. An analyst cited about INR 4 crore for Q4, which management did not reconcile on the call.

guidance_outlook: Cost initiatives target about INR 150 crore for FY27: INR 29 crore realised in April-May, with another INR 120 crore expected over the next 10 months, dependent on commodity and forex.
Management is aspiring to grow home appliances more than 20% in FY27 but described it as a stretch; first two months' revenue described as on track.

Engineering plans 20-25% growth over 2-3 years on existing business plus new verticals (EV battery parts, motorcycle chains, brake discs), with FY27 target about 23% revenue growth and INR 350 crore of new order additions.
Home appliance capex of INR 20-30 crore for capacity expansion in front loader, top loader and AC lines; about 50% of home appliance investment is on 13 kg and 14 kg front loader platforms.
Price increases taken in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 across almost all categories; further increases to be assessed against competitive position.
AC market share aspiration of double digits, described as a tough ask this year.
Import content of manufacturing is about 30%, targeted to fall to about 25%; total imports at 39%, targeted at 30-32%.
capex_capacity: Engineering: about INR 100 crore capex approved last year, of which INR 63 crore implemented to March, carried into FY27. Three presses added to stamping, adding INR 40-50 crore revenue capacity; fine blanking press added at each of Kolkata and Bangalore, each worth INR 30-40 crore.

Engineering: a new chain manufacturing site is being identified. Schmid Automotive Appliances, a Switzerland tooling subsidiary incorporated in December, is about 5-6 months old and has taken orders from a Spanish company.
Home Appliances: capex of about INR 43 crore in FY26 out of INR 88.6 crore company-wide. About INR 500 crore of total capex over the last five to six years per analyst.
Home Appliances: 13 kg and 14 kg front loader launches planned this year; 12 kg (about 13% of the market) not currently operated.
demand_pricing: Front loader market share about 23% overall, or about 25.5-26% excluding the 12 kg segment; top loader share about 9%, with top loader market share rising.
AC market share about 3-3.5%; the segment is more fragmented.
Refrigeration volume and value growth described as good from a low base.
Distribution focus on about 10,000-10,500 outlets that account for about 80% of volumes; in-store promoters increased by about 400-500.
AC energy-rating transition effective 1 January 2026 caused cost per unit increases and liquidation; INR 7 crore impact in FY26, of which about INR 6 crore in Q4.
Portfolio rationalisation: front loader models cut from 58 to 25, with similar cuts in top loaders; management says revenue growth is running well ahead of volume growth in most segments.
Some large OEM AC customers have stopped buying; management said OEM revenue was down about 5% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 revenue breakdown by AC, front load and top load, and whether front load unit sales reconcile with revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give category revenue splits; the 21% front loader growth in Q4 refers to industry 12 kg-and-above data, not company units. Company front loader growth was about 7-8% for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 84 crore commodity and forex hit was recovered, and does it reverse next year?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 67 crore was recovered in FY26 via cost initiatives and price increases. Management expects INR 120 crore more from cost initiatives over 10 months, with the P&L benefit from any commodity or forex easing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity and forex hit so far in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: April-May commodity and forex headwind is about INR 49 crore; INR 29 crore has been offset by cost initiatives, leaving about INR 20 crore to be recovered through price increases.

qa_highlights.question: How far is engineering's capex and growth path, and what are the target margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue CAGR of about 13% over five years; plan is 20-25% growth over 2-3 years with EBITDA margin of 17-18% from about 15% today. Only INR 63 crore of INR 100 crore approved capex was implemented, carried into FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY26 engineering order wins INR 153 crore against a INR 250 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Order conversion takes 7-8 months of validation; the RFQ pipeline is active and management expects closures by Q1 or early Q2 FY27, targeting about INR 350 crore of additions for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Did fixed cost savings materialise in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing substantial has moved into the P&L; fixed cost review (advertising, travel) is a lower priority than bigger variable cost items.

risks_watch: Commodity and forex headwinds: INR 49 crore in April-May, with recovery dependent on price increases and cost initiatives reaching INR 120 crore more over 10 months.
Management said it cannot pass through all raw material inflation given competitive position, so incremental margin expansion looks constrained.
Import dependence: about 39% overall import content, with indigenisation targeted to bring it to 30-32%.
Engineering order conversion lag and the FY26 order-win shortfall (INR 153 crore vs INR 250 crore target).
AC market share and OEM volume: key large OEM customers have stopped buying; AC share is about 3-3.5% against a double-digit aspiration.
Leadership transition: new Home Appliances MD and CEO joined 8 April 2026; Chairman unwell and absent from the call.
Disclosure gaps: category revenue splits, inventory days and the refrigeration associate outlook were not provided on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and market share, with the new Home Appliances CEO calling revenue momentum 'on track' and describing the market as buoyant. Cautious on margins: commodity and forex costs are not fully recovered, and several answers (category splits, fixed costs, refrigeration, OEM sales) were deferred or non-specific.
